Rashi on Gittin 4b:11:1.hebrew: לעולם ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל לא צריך - כדקא דייקת, ולא תיקשי לרבא:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:11:1.english: Indeed, from region to region within Eretz Yisrael he is not required - As you inferred, and this should not pose a difficulty for Rava.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:12:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים - שכיחי עדים לקיימו. והא דאמרן לעיל בריש שמעתין "ממדינה למדינה בא"י איכא בינייהו" — ליתא, וסמי ליה מהכא:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:12:1.english: Since there are pilgrims - Witnesses are frequently available to validate it. And as for what we said above at the beginning of this discussion, "from region to region in Eretz Yisrael is [the difference] between them" — this is not [the correct text], and erase it from here.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:13:1.hebrew: בתי דינין דקבועין - בעיירות, כתקנת עזרא, בשני ובה': ומצויות שיירות שהולכות לדון במקום הוועד:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:13:1.english: Courts that are fixed - In the towns, as per the ordinance of Ezra, on Monday and Thursday; and caravans that go to be judged at the place of assembly are common.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:14:1.hebrew: מקפידין זה על זה - שלא ילך בן הגמוניא זו להגמוניא זו:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:14:1.english: Particular with each other - That a resident of this district should not go to that district.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:15:1.hebrew: לרבה קשיא - דהא ארץ ישראל הואי, ובקיאין לשמה, ומשום דלא שכיחי לקיימו אצרכוה:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:15:1.english: According to Rabba it is difficult - For it is Eretz Yisrael, and [its residents] are well versed in [the requirement that a get be written] for her sake; and [so the reason must be] because [witnesses] are not available to ratify it, [and nevertheless] they required [the declaration].

Rashi on Gittin 4b:15:2.hebrew: רבה אית ליה דרבא - דממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל, היכא דקפדי ולא שכיחי עדים, צריך למימר. אבל רבא לית ליה דרבה, דאי שכיחי עדים לא חיישינן לאין בקיאין, דכולהו בקיאין:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:15:2.english: Rabbah holds like Rava - [He agrees that] from district to district in Eretz Yisrael, where they are particular and witnesses are not readily available, one must say [the declaration]. But Rava does not hold like Rabbah, for if witnesses are readily available, we do not worry about [people] not being expert, since all of them are expert.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:16:1.hebrew: אלא מאי בינייהו - אתרוייהו שינויי מהדר, אשינויא קמא דשנינן "כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים כו'", ותו ליכא למימר "ממדינה למדינה מצריך רבא" בין אשינויא דאמרינן דרבה. היכא דקפדי, מודי בה דבעינן נמי לקיימו, ומהשתא ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל לא איפליגו בה, דאי קפדי מודה בה רבה, דהא אית ליה דרבא, ואי לא קפדי מודי בה רבא, דהא שכיחי לקיימו משום קביעותא דבתי דינין. ומאי בינייהו? כלומר, חסרו להו הנך טעמי דאוקימנא פלוגתייהו לעיל? ומשני: ודאי חסרי להו, וסמי חד מינייהו, ופשו להו תרי טעמי באותה מדינה במדינת הים, והיכא דאתיוה בי תרי ממדינת הים, רבה מצריך, רבא לא מצריך:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:16:1.english: Rather, what is [the difference] between them - [The Gemara] goes back over both answers: over the first answer that we gave, "Since there are pilgrims, etc.", and further, it cannot be said that "from country to country Rava requires [it]", as against the answer that we said is Rabba's. Where they are particular, [Rava] agrees that we also need to have [the document] validated; and from now on, [regarding a document brought] from country to country within the Land of Israel, they do not disagree about it: for if they are particular, Rabba agrees to it, since he holds Rava's view; and if they are not particular, Rava agrees to it, since [witnesses] are readily available to validate it, because of the permanence of the courts. And [the Gemara asks] "What is [the difference] between them?", that is to say, do those reasons by which we established their dispute above fall short for them? And it answers: Certainly they fall short for them, and one of them is removed, and two reasons remain for them with respect to that country, [a country] overseas. And where two [people] brought it from overseas, Rabba requires [the declaration], [while] Rava does not require [it].

Rashi on Gittin 4b:18:1.hebrew: ואינו יכול - מפרש ואזיל מאי היא:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:18:1.english: And he is unable - [The Gemara] goes on to explain what it is.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:18:2.hebrew: יתקיים בחותמיו - יבאו המכירים החתימה, וכשר:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:18:2.english: It shall be ratified by its signatories - Those who recognize the signature shall come, and it is valid.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:1:1.english: And these are learned - [i.e., they are learned in the law] of Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:5:1.hebrew: לפרושי טעמא דתנא קמא - דאיהו נמי מוליך ומביא ס"ל, אלא חד מינייהו נקט:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:5:1.english: To explain the reasoning of the first tanna - For he too holds [that the declaration applies to] one who takes [the bill of divorce] and one who brings [it]; rather, he mentioned only one of them.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:6:1.english: But within the same region - and from city to city.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:6:2.hebrew: לא צריך - ואע"ג דאין בקיאין לשמה, הואיל ועדים מצויין לקיימו, לא צריך:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:6:2.english: He is not required - Even though they are not experts in [writing it] for its own sake, since witnesses are available to authenticate it, he is not required [to say this].

Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:1.english: If from that - From the inference of the first clause.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:2.hebrew: הוה אמינא הני מילי דיעבד - דאי מייתי ממדינה למדינה בא"י ולא נכתב לפניו, אין צריך ליפסול שליחותו על כך:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:2.english: I would have said that this applies only after the fact - For if he brings [a bill of divorce] from one place to another within Eretz Yisrael, and it was not written in his presence, there is no need to disqualify his agency on this account.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:3.hebrew: אבל לכתחילה - אי הוה מימליך, הוה מורינן ליה דליקו עליה:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:3.english: But ab initio - If he had consulted [us], we would have instructed him that he should stand [and say the declaration] over it.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:8:4.english: It teaches us - The superfluous mishna of the latter clause, which is not needed.

Rashi on Gittin 4b:9:1.hebrew: ואיכא דמותיב הכי כו' - וניחא ליה למידק מרישא ולאותובי, ולאו לאותובי מסיפא דקתני בהדיא "המביא גט בארץ ישראל אינו צריך", אלמא טעמא משום לשמה הוא. דמשום דברישא תני בהדיא "ממדינה למדינה", וסיפא לא תנא "ממדינה למדינה", ואי הוה מותיב ליה מיניה, הוה משני ליה דבאותה מדינה עצמה קאי. ואע"ג דהוה מותבינן ליה מכלל דמדינת הים באותה מדינה נמי לא צריך, סוף סוף הדר הוה ליה דוקיא:
Rashi on Gittin 4b:9:1.english: And there are those who raise the objection thus, etc. - It is preferable to him to infer from the first clause and to raise the objection from it, and not to raise the objection from the latter clause, which explicitly teaches, "One who brings a bill of divorce in Eretz Yisrael is not required [to make the declaration]," [from which one might say] that evidently the reason is because of [the requirement that it be written] for its own sake. [He avoids the latter clause] because in the first clause it explicitly teaches "from region to region," whereas the latter clause does not teach "from region to region." And if he were to raise the objection from it, [the other] would answer him that [the latter clause refers to one who] stands in that very same region. And even though we would be raising the objection against him by implication — that overseas, too, within that same region [the declaration] is not required — in the end it would again be a forced [reading].

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:12:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים מישכח שכיחי - ואע"ג דלענין מחאה שלא בפניו אמרינן בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לח:): סתם יהודה וגליל כשעת חירום דמי, ולא הוי מחאה — היינו משום שאין המחזיק דרכו לחזר אם עשו מחאה. אבל הכא שמחזרת אחר עדים המכירים חתימת העדים, מצויין לקיימו. ואם תאמר: דלקמן (גיטין דף ו.) משמע איפכא, גבי בני מחוזא דניידי ומצרכי "בפני נכתב" משכונה לשכונה — אטו במחוזא מי לא הוה מחאה? וי"ל: דהתם אפילו ימחה בפני בני אדם שהולכין להם שלא יאמרו למחזיק, מכל מקום דרך הליכתם יאמרו לאחרים, "וחברך חברא אית ליה", כדאמרינן התם. אבל לענין קיום, כיון דניידי, לא ימצא קיום כשיצטרך להם:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:12:1.english: Since there are pilgrims, they are readily available - And even though with regard to protest not in the [possessor's] presence we say in [the chapter] Chezkat Habatim (Bava Batra 38b): Ordinarily, Judea and the Galilee are like a time of emergency, and it is not considered a protest — that is because the possessor does not usually go around [to find out] whether they made a protest. But here, where she goes around seeking witnesses who recognize the signatures of the [document's] witnesses, they are readily available to authenticate it. And if you say: Later (Gittin 6a) it implies the opposite, regarding the people of Mechoza, who are mobile, and they require [the declaration] "in my presence it was written" from neighborhood to neighborhood — is it the case that in Mechoza there would not be a protest? And one can answer: There, even if he protests in front of people who are going their way, [telling them] not to tell the possessor, in any event, in the course of their travels they will tell others, [for] "your friend has a friend," as we say there. But with regard to authentication, since they are mobile, authentication will not be found when she needs them.

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:14:1.hebrew: ואמר ר' יצחק עיר אחת היתה בארץ ישראל כו' - בלא ר' יצחק נמי יש להוכיח דבארץ ישראל היתה, דבחוצה לארץ באותה הגמוניא נמי צריך לרבה, כיון דאין בקיאין לשמה:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:14:1.english: "And Rabbi Yitzchak said: There was one city in Eretz Yisrael," etc. - Even without [the statement of] Rabbi Yitzchak, it can be proven that [the city] was in Eretz Yisrael, for [if it had been] outside of Eretz Yisrael, [the declaration] would be required, according to Rabba, even within the same district, since they are not well versed in [the requirement that it be written and signed] for her sake.

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:14:2.english: That they were particular with each other - And their cherum (blockade) was greater than the cherum between Judea and the Galilee:

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:15:1.hebrew: רבה אית ליה דרבא - וא"ת: אמאי צריך לרבה "בפני נכתב" מהגמוניא להגמוניא? והא רבה לא חייש לאיחלופי, כיון דידענו — לא מהני. וי"ל: דמתחילה לא היו מתקנין "בפני נכתב" משום איחלופי, אבל כיון דתקינו משום לשמה במדינת הים, תקנו שיאמר בכל מקום, אף בארץ ישראל:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:15:1.english: Rabba holds like Rava - And if you ask: Why, according to Rabba, is it necessary [to say] "in my presence it was written" from one province (hegemonia) to another? Rabba does not worry about mix-ups (iḥlufei), since we know [the law], it does not help. And one can answer: Originally they did not enact [the declaration] "in my presence it was written" because of mix-ups. But once they enacted it because of [the requirement that the get be written] for her sake in overseas lands, they enacted that it be said everywhere, even in Eretz Yisrael:

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:16:1.hebrew: אלא מאי בינייהו - לעיל כי משני: כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים מישכח שכיחי, לא הוה מצי למיבעי מאי בינייהו, דאכתי איכא בינייהו: מקומות דלא קביעי בתי דינין, או שמקפידין זה על זה:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:16:1.english: Rather, what is the difference between them? - Above, when [the Gemara] answered, "Since there are pilgrims, [witnesses] are readily found," it could not have asked, "What is the difference between them?" For there would still be a difference between them: [in] places where courts are not established, or [where the courts] are particular about one another.

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:6:1.hebrew: תנן המביא גט ממדינה למדינה במדינת הים - ומרישא דמתניתין: "המביא גט ממדינת הים", דמשמע דוקא ממדינת הים לארץ ישראל — לא מצי למיפרך, דלעולם באותה מדינה במדינת הים נמי צריך; ונקט הכי לאפוקי רקם וחגר:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:6:1.english: We learned: "One who brings a bill of divorce from one region to another region within a country overseas" - And from the first clause of the mishna, "One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas," which implies specifically from overseas to Eretz Yisrael — [the Gemara] could not object, for in truth, within the same region in a country overseas he is also required [to make the declaration]; and [the Tanna] phrased it this way to exclude Rekem and Heger.

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:7:1.hebrew: אלא אימא ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל לא צריך - וא"ת: ואמאי נקט ממדינה למדינה? ניתני: "המביא גט באותה מדינה במדינת הים צריך" כו', הא בארץ ישראל אין צריך באותה מדינה, וה"ה ממדינה למדינה, דלרבה אין חילוק בין אותה מדינה ובין ממדינה למדינה! וי"ל דנקט הכי לאשמועינן, דלא נימא דממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל צריך נמי משום קיום כרבא; קמ"ל דאין צריך, דטעמא לאו משום קיום. אי נמי משום דשכיחי עולי רגלים, כדמסיק:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:7:1.english: Rather, say: From region to region in Eretz Yisrael, he is not required [to make the declaration] - And if you ask: Why did [the mishna] state "from region to region"? Let it teach: "One who brings a get within the same region, in a country overseas, must [make the declaration]," etc., [and from this we would learn that] in Eretz Yisrael, within the same region he need not, and the same applies from region to region, since according to Rabbah there is no distinction between within the same region and from region to region! And one can answer that it stated it this way to teach us, so that we should not say that from region to region in Eretz Yisrael he is also required, because of [the need for] confirmation (kiyum), in accordance with Rava. [Therefore] it teaches us that he is not required, for the reason is not because of confirmation. Alternatively, [the reason is] because pilgrims [to Jerusalem] are common, as [the Gemara] concludes.

Tosafot on Gittin 4b:8:1.hebrew: אי מההיא הוה אמינא הני מילי דיעבד - פירש בקונטרס: אי מדיוקא דרישא. ופי' כן משום דאסיפא לא הוי מצי למימר "הני מילי דיעבד", דהא בהדיא קתני "אין צריך", דמשמע לכתחילה. ומיהו לשון "אי מההיא" לא משמע הכי. ונראה דיש ליישב, דהכא שייך למיתני "א"צ" בדיעבד, כלומר: אין צריך ליטלו הימנה כשלא אמר "בפני נכתב ובפ"נ", דאמר לקמן: כיצד יעשה? יטלנו הימנה ויחזור ויתן לה בפני שנים, ויאמר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם". אבל קשה, דאמרינן בריש פ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף טו.): המביא גט ממדינת הים ואמר "בפני נכתב" אבל לא "בפני נחתם" כו' — פסול. ופריך בגמ': תנינא חדא זימנא "המביא" כו'. ומשני: אי מההיא הוה אמינא צריך, ואי לא אמר — כשר. והיכי הוה מצי למימר הכי? הא אמרינן הכא דאי לא תנא אלא חד בבא, הוה אמינא בא"י לכתחילה צריך; מכלל דבמדינת הים אפילו בדיעבד נמי צריך! וי"ל דמאחר דתנא הכא תרי בבי לאשמועינן דארץ ישראל אפילו לכתחילה אין צריך, אם כן מהשתא מצינן למימר דהא דצריך במדינת הים היינו לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד כשר. להכי איצטריך מתניתין דפ"ב. ועוד נראה לר"י דהכי פירושא: "הני מילי דיעבד" שלא ראה כתיבת הגט וחתימתו, דיכול ליתנו לה בא"י; אבל לכתחילה צריך שיראה כתיבת הגט וחתימתו, כדי שיוכל לומר "בפני נכתב". קמ"ל דלא צריך. ובמדינת הים, אם לא ראה כתיבת הגט וחתימתו, אין יכול להביאו וליתנו לה; ואם הביא ונתנו — ה"א דכשר, אי לא מתניתין דפ"ב. והשתא מיתרצה נמי פירכא קמייתא:
Tosafot on Gittin 4b:8:1.english: "If [it were derived] from that, I would have said: this applies only after the fact" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: [This means,] if from the inference of the first clause. And he explained it this way because regarding the latter clause, [the Gemara] could not have said "this applies only after the fact," since [the mishna] explicitly teaches "he is not required [to say]," which implies even ab initio. However, the wording "if from that" does not imply this. And it appears that one can resolve [this], for here it is relevant for [the mishna] to teach "he is not required" in the after-the-fact sense, meaning: he is not required to take it back from her if he did not say "in my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed," as [the mishna] says later: What should he do? He takes it back from her, and then gives it to her again in the presence of two [witnesses], and says, "In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed." But this is difficult, for we say at the beginning of the second chapter (later, Gittin 15a): One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas and says, "In my presence it was written," but not "in my presence it was signed," etc. — it is invalid. And the Gemara asks: We already learned once, "One who brings," etc. And it answers: If [it were derived] from that, I would have said it is required, but if he did not say it, [the bill of divorce] is valid. But how could [the Gemara] say this? We say here that if [the mishna] had taught only one clause, I would have said that in Eretz Yisrael it is required ab initio; by implication, overseas it is required even after the fact! And one can answer that since [the mishna] teaches two clauses here to inform us that in Eretz Yisrael he is not required [to say it] even ab initio, it follows that now we can say that what is required overseas is ab initio, but after the fact it is valid. Therefore the mishna of the second chapter is needed. Furthermore, it appears to the Ri that this is the explanation: "This applies only after the fact" — where he did not see the writing of the bill of divorce and its signing, [in which case] he can give it to her in Eretz Yisrael; but ab initio, he must see the writing of the bill of divorce and its signing, so that he can say "in my presence it was written." [The mishna] teaches us that this is not required. And overseas, if he did not see the writing of the bill of divorce and its signing, he cannot bring it and give it to her; and if he brought it and gave it, I would have thought it is valid, were it not for the mishna of the second chapter. And now the first difficulty is also resolved.
